mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes the epidermal tissue system in flowering plants?

options.A: It forms the outermost protective layer covering all aerial parts of the plant.
options.B: It consists mainly of xylem and phloem for transport.
options.C: It stores food reserves and provides structural support.
options.D: It is responsible for photosynthesis in leaf mesophyll.

mcqs.answer: It forms the outermost protective layer covering all aerial parts of the plant.
mcqs.explanation: The epidermal tissue system is the outermost layer of cells that protects the plant and reduces water loss. It does not conduct water (vascular), store food (ground), or perform photosynthesis (mesophyll).

mcqs.question: What are the primary functions of the ground tissue system in flowering plants?

options.A: Conduct water and minerals throughout the plant.
options.B: Protect the plant from pathogen invasion.
options.C: Perform photosynthesis, store food, and provide structural support.

mcqs.answer: Perform photosynthesis, store food, and provide structural support.
mcqs.explanation: Ground tissue includes parenchyma (photosynthesis and storage), collenchyma (flexible support), and sclerenchyma (rigid support). It does not conduct water (vascular) or directly protect against pathogens (dermal).

mcqs.question: Which definition correctly distinguishes the vascular tissue system from other tissue systems?

options.A: It is composed of epidermal cells that secrete cuticle.
options.B: It consists of parenchyma cells that store starch.
options.C: It comprises xylem and phloem that conduct water, minerals, and organic nutrients.
options.D: It is made up of collenchyma cells that provide flexible support.

mcqs.answer: It comprises xylem and phloem that conduct water, minerals, and organic nutrients.
mcqs.explanation: Vascular tissue is specialized for transport: xylem moves water and minerals upward, while phloem distributes sugars and other organic compounds. The other options describe epidermal, ground, or supportive tissues.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate tissue systems to plant organs
mcqs.question: In which plant organ is the dermal tissue system most prominently involved in protecting against water loss?
mcqs.explanation: Leaves have a thick cuticle and stomata that are part of the epidermal (dermal) tissue system, crucial for minimizing transpiration. Roots are covered by a periderm, flowers have specialized epidermis, and seeds have seed coats.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is an example of a specialized epidermal cell in the leaf?
mcqs.explanation: Guard cells are modified epidermal cells that regulate stomatal opening. Xylem vessels belong to vascular tissue, sclerenchyma fibers to ground tissue, and parenchyma cells are also ground tissue.

mcqs.question: A farmer observes that the tubers of a crop plant are enlarged and rich in starch. Which type of ground tissue is primarily responsible for this storage function?
mcqs.explanation: Parenchyma cells are thin‑walled, living ground tissue that store starch, oils, and other reserves. Collenchyma provides flexible support, sclerenchyma provides rigidity, and meristematic tissue is involved in growth, not storage.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the vascular tissue system is a common misconception?

options.A: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals from roots to shoots.
options.B: Phloem transports organic nutrients from sources to sinks.
options.C: Xylem also transports minerals along with water.
options.D: Xylem transports sugars produced by photosynthesis.

mcqs.answer: Xylem transports sugars produced by photosynthesis.
mcqs.explanation: Xylem transports only water and inorganic minerals; sugars are transported by phloem. Option D reflects the misconception that xylem carries sugars.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate tissue systems to plant organs
mcqs.question: A young stem must remain flexible to bend with wind without breaking. Which tissue system contributes most to this flexibility?
mcqs.explanation: Collenchyma, a component of the ground tissue system, has unevenly thickened walls that provide flexibility while supporting growth. Dermal tissue protects, vascular tissue provides transport and rigidity, and there is no reproductive tissue in stems.
